question.question: After successful valid InstallSnapshot covers the receiver last-log index, must an otherwise valid current-term AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry at that boundary validate against the installed snapshot term rather than an obsolete retained log term?
question.importance: Incorrect rejection at the recovery boundary can prevent a follower from resuming log replication and hence reduce available quorum participation. This consequence is potential; only local predecessor validation is obligated here.
contexts: No storage errors or intervening role/history changes; snapshot index equals old log end
Valid majority-committed snapshot may supersede an uncommitted divergent suffix

obligation.description: After a valid snapshot has successfully installed and restored through the receiver previous log end, predecessor validation for a subsequent otherwise valid current-term AppendEntries at exactly that snapshot index must use the installed snapshot term. A superseded retained log term at that index must not cause rejection.

scope.description: Receiver snapshot-boundary consumption for normal protocol-v3 snapshot-v1 transfer. Snapshot boundary equals the pre-install last-log index, with either equal or different prior term. The following append is from the same current leader, contiguous and storage-successful.
assumptions: Snapshot represents valid committed leader history and replaces only uncommitted divergent receiver suffix.
Stable membership, correct leader, deterministic successful FSM restore and storage, no concurrent transition between install completion and append.
excluded: Proof of whole-cluster liveness or an infinite retry cycle
Client operation deadline or quorum endpoint
Administrative Restore and corrupt/malicious snapshot bytes

grounding.derivation: InstallSnapshotRequest defines LastLogIndex/Term as the included snapshot boundary; README specifies snapshot restoration equivalence to replay of old logs. The TODO test plan in raft_test.go explicitly requires checking the snapshot term for a predecessor exactly at the snapshot index. That TODO is an intended expectation, not an executed passing test. Together with the producer setPreviousLog using snapshot term after successful snapshot transfer, these ground a receiver consistency responsibility. The equal-index cache choice is the observed implementation discrepancy, not the normative source.
grounding.applicability: Valid snapshot supersedes the uncommitted old suffix and completed restore precedes the append. Requirement concerns which history boundary is consumed, not eventual progress or success under unrelated errors.
alternatives: Retaining physical old log entries for trailing-log policy is allowed; treating an obsolete term as authoritative at the restored boundary is the issue.
